articles.title: Details of thousands of US immigration agents leaked in major hack
articles.summary: A group called the Department of Peace released information on more than 41,000 DHS staff.
articles.body:
Details of more than 41,000 personnel working for the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including thousands involved in immigration enforcement, have been leaked to the public.

The leak includes names, work addresses and phone numbers of DHS staff, including agents working with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection, along with descriptions of the work they do for each agency.

Wednesday's leak marks the third time in recent weeks that a government agency has been targeted by leaks or hacks.

A DHS spokesperson said the agency is "aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively."

"We take all security threats against our employees and officers seriously and will work to ensure all are properly protected," the spokesperson added.

"We will update the public when more information is available."

The seemingly unprecedented breach of employee information was made public online. A group called the Department of Peace accessed the information from DHS, while journalist and cybersecurity researcher maia crimew alongside the website Distributed Denial of Secrets put it online.

The information was put in a database named Icepick.

Most of the agents included, more than 21,000 of them, work for CBP, according to the data. Nearly 6,600 work for ICE.

Other records show agents with Homeland Security Investigations, the Federal Protective Service and even people working for the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.

The leaked information also included dozens of previously unknown operation names, the agents that led and worked on those operations, and some of the technology they used in their work, including tech provided by Cellbrite and Palantir.

The groups wrote in an online statement that the the leak was not meant to be a directory of every DHS agent. Rather the aim was to replace "anonymity with accountability", according to Emma Best, a co founder of DDoSecrets.

"The leak is extraordinary but deceptive in it's simplicity as it identifies the officials responsible for overseeing covert and undercover operations, the government's hunt for leakers and the failed BlueLeaks investigation - along with key personnel in DHS's ever-escalating rendition and deportation programs," Best added.

BlueLeaks refers to a massive leak of US police data in 2020, data from which DDoSecrets also hosted.

A spokesperson for the Department of Peace pointed directly at actions by ICE agents for the groups work to hack DHS records.

"On July 17th, Markwayne Mullin said he was 'turning up the heat'. This is what happens to ICE when you do that," the spokesperson wrote on Wednesday.

Mullin in March became Secretary of Homeland Security.

The Department of Peace said it accessed the DHS agent profiles through a single sign-on service called Okta.

Okta is a popular online security tool that organisations use to ensure that only people with access to internal platforms are logging on to them.

A spokeswoman for Okta said the company is aware of the claims being made, but said: "Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised."

Last month, the FBI was hacked by a group called ShinyHunters, which took personal information about thousands of agents.

In recent days, the Federal Election Commission, which makes public political campaign donation data, was taken offline because of a suspected hacking attempt.

Public backlash to US immigration enforcement has been building as the Trump Administration has pushed a huge increase in arrests and deportations of people suspected of being in the country illegally.

Immigration operations this year have repeatedly turned violent , with ICE agents shooting at more than two dozen people and killing at least nine people.

Those killings include the high profile deaths of Alex Pretti and Renee Good, both of whom were shot and killed by ICE agents this year in Minnesota, despite not being the targets of arrests.

Often, ICE agents carry out enforcement actions while their faces are covered by masks and sunglasses. Immigration agents rarely identify themselves, despite being required by law to do so, and US politicians have publicly demanded DHS enforces the requirement.

Since President Donald Trump returned to office in 2025, the US has enacted nearly 1 million deportations , according to data from the Migration Policy Institute. More than 70% of the deportations have been of people with no criminal record.

articles.title: In 2009, Bob Dylan donated his US royalties from a Christmas album to Feeding America and pledged international earnings to charities helping people facing hunger and homelessness
articles.summary: In 2009, Bob Dylan released a Christmas album with a charitable commitment that extended beyond the holiday season.
articles.body: In 2009, Bob Dylan released a Christmas album with a charitable commitment that extended beyond the holiday season. The singer-songwriter pledged all his US royalties from Christmas in the Heart to Feeding America, with the initial donation expected to provide more than 4 million meals to over 1.4 million people in need. The project also supported 2 international organisations: the World Food Programme (WFP), which provides food assistance around the world, and Crisis, a UK charity working with people experiencing homelessness. Dylan committed future royalties from the album to the organisations in perpetuity. Released in the US on October 13, 2009, the album paired familiar Christmas songs with a fundraising effort spanning the United States, the United Kingdom and the developing world.Christmas in the Heart: how Bob Dylan directed his US royalties to Feeding AmericaChristmas in the Heart was billed by Dylan’s official website as his 47th album. It followed Together Through Life, released earlier in 2009, and was his first Christmas album, featuring traditional carols and popular holiday songs, including “Here Comes Santa Claus”, “Winter Wonderland”, “Little Drummer Boy” and “Must Be Santa”. The announcement on Dylan’s website confirmed that all his US royalties from sales of the album would go to Feeding America. The initial contribution was expected to provide more than 4 million meals to over 1.4 million people during the 2009 holiday season. Dylan also committed all future US royalties from the album to the organisation in perpetuity. At the time, Feeding America described itself as the largest domestic hunger-relief charity in the United States. Its network included more than 200 member food banks supporting 63,000 agencies, which helped distribute food to people facing hunger across the country. The organisation reported serving more than 25 million Americans annually, including 9 million children and 3 million seniors.Dylan explained the motivation behind his contribution by pointing to the scale of hunger in the United States. He said it was a tragedy that more than 35 million people, including 12 million children, often went to bed hungry and faced uncertainty about where their next meal would come from. He expressed hope that the initiative would help bring greater food security to people in need. Vicki Escarra, Feeding America’s president and chief executive at the time, said the organisation had not anticipated that Dylan would donate all his royalties from the forthcoming album. She also noted that the initiative could raise awareness of hunger in the United States and elsewhere.World Food Programme and Crisis: where the international royalties wentDylan’s charitable commitment also covered international royalties. A September 2009 announcement on his official website identified the World Food Programme and Crisis as recipients of international royalties from Christmas in the Heart. Both organisations were to receive support in perpetuity. The initial contributions had specific targets. WFP was expected to provide 500,000 meals to schoolchildren in the developing world during the holiday season. Crisis was expected to provide 15,000 meals to people experiencing homelessness in the United Kingdom.WFP was confronting a substantial global hunger crisis in 2009. A UN briefing dated September 24, 2009 reported that WFP’s executive director, Josette Sheeran, had welcomed Dylan’s contribution. The briefing said the hunger crisis threatened 108 million people worldwide. WFP had also said it was aiming to feed 108 million people in 74 countries that year, according to a UN briefing on September 16, 2009. Crisis worked with people experiencing homelessness in the UK. articles.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has identified three nations currently leading the globe in manufacturing and technology while also explaining why the US did not make his list, during a recent discussion with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Addressing China's industrial strengths, Huang pointed out that Beijing holds a unique competitive edge because its modern economic transformation directly coincided with the rise of the digital era. According to Huang, the global powers in production and advanced technology has revolved around three specific countries: Germany, Japan and China.“For the last 50 years, because of the current Industrial Revolution, which is computing and digital technology, the United States has largely exported its heavy manufacturing, its building, and its craft to China. So now the world has three (leaders) again. It’s Germany, Japan and China,” Huang said.Why China did not make it to Huang’s listHuang highlighted that China’s advantage stems from critical timing. Since its industrial surge unfolded alongside the rise of computing, its manufacturing base developed with digital infrastructure integrated from the start, leaving the country heavily computerised.“The advantage that China has is that they came into their industrial revolution, if you will, their economic transformation happened during precisely the time of the computer industry. They are quite computerized. China is probably the only nation today that is deep in manufacturing and deep in computer science. And very comfortable in both,” he highlighted.US restrictions pushed China’s progressSpeaking to CNBC on the sidelines of Nvidia's GTC Berlin conference, the Nvidia CEO said that export curbs and trade restrictions imposed by the US have pushed China to speed up its own domestic chip manufacturing and strive for technological self-reliance.Current US trade rules prohibit the export of advanced processors to China, including Nvidia's high-end artificial intelligence (AI) GPUs. Reports have claimed that several Chinese entities have managed to access that computing power through third-party data centers based in Southeast Asia.“We’ve definitely accelerated China’s initiatives, its nationalization of semiconductor manufacturing capabilities, and all of the industrial support that has been put into that sector, and so there’s no question we’ve accelerated that,” Huang said.Huang, however, said that despite intensified competition and China’s accelerated domestic initiatives, American tech firms remain well-prepared to take on competitive pressure “from anybody.”You use AI every day. articles.summary: Hundreds of people living aboard a cruise ship that had been travelling around the world for more than two years were forced to disembark in Cambodia
articles.body: Hundreds of people living aboard a cruise ship that had been travelling around the world for more than two years were forced to disembark in Cambodia after its operator suspended operations, citing soaring fuel costs linked to the Iran war.The owner of the Villa Vie Odyssey, Villa Vie Residences, announced on Tuesday that it was suspending operations and disembarking passengers in Cambodia while working to arrange temporary accommodation for them, Reuters reported.Monthly fuel expenses, which had historically averaged around $1,800 per cabin, have recently risen to an estimated $6,000 to $8,000 in parts of Asia, the company said in a statement.“The company cannot simply pass increases of that scale on to residents, and the resulting shortfall has placed its current operating model under unsustainable financial pressure,” it said.The ship had been cruising the world for at least 755 days, offering passengers the option to rent or buy long-term or permanent residences on board. It can accommodate up to 650 people, although its rooms were still being filled. Reuters reported.The vessel had 203 passengers and 156 crew members on board, deputy governor of Cambodia’s Preah Sihanouk province, Long Dimanche, said. Some passengers had already left on flights, while others were waiting in the port city of Sihanoukville, he told the media.The ship is scheduled to refuel before leaving Cambodia on Saturday, Dimanche added.According to Reuters, accommodation options on the vessel include an inside villa priced at $120,000 and “villa suites” costing $440,000.The company said it had taken steps to reduce fuel consumption since the Iran war began in late February, including slowing the ship’s itinerary and spending more time in port. However, these measures were insufficient to offset what it described as an “extraordinary” increase in fuel costs.“We have been unable to continue carrying the resulting operating losses,” the company said, adding that it would seek to restructure and recapitalise over the next 60 days. articles.title: A 39-year-old Florida climber spent two nights in freezing conditions after falling into a crevasse on California’s Mount Shasta; with helicopter access blocked by 60 mph winds, rescuers reached him on foot and carried him out
articles.summary: A 39-year-old man from Florida has been rescued from California’s Mount Shasta after spending two nights stranded on a glacier with a serious leg injury,
articles.body: A 39-year-old man from Florida has been rescued from California’s Mount Shasta after spending two nights stranded on a glacier with a serious leg injury, as freezing temperatures and powerful winds prevented rescuers from evacuating him by helicopter. Reports by CBS Sacramento, the San Francisco Chronicle and SFGATE detailed the multiday operation, which involved U.S. Forest Service climbing rangers and more than 30 additional search-and-rescue personnel. The climber was brought to safety on Tuesday, October 20, after a rescue team carried him across hazardous mountain terrain to a location where a helicopter could reach him. He was subsequently taken to hospital for treatment of his leg injury and frostbite affecting his foot and leg.How the climber became stranded on Mount ShastaAccording to the Siskiyou County Sheriff's Office and the U.S. Forest Service, the man reached the 14,179-foot summit of Mount Shasta at around 3 p.m. on Sunday, October 18. He was descending via the Avalanche Gulch route when an incorrect GPS route led him towards Whitney Glacier, on the mountain's northern side.At approximately 12,600 feet, he fell through a snow bridge covering a crevasse and fractured his leg. Unable to continue safely, he called 911 at around 5 p.m., prompting authorities to launch a search-and-rescue operation.The climber was poorly equipped for the conditions. Officials said he was wearing sweatpants, a sweatshirt and running shoes, with only trekking poles and limited food and water. He did not have the appropriate clothing or equipment for an unexpected overnight stay in the high mountains. Temperatures on the glacier dropped below freezing, while strong winds and poor visibility made it difficult for rescue teams to reach him before nightfall.Rescuers spent a night on the mountain with himTwo U.S. Forest Service climbing rangers eventually reached the injured man on Monday morning. They provided medical assistance, including treatment for frostbite and the onset of hypothermia, and helped him move away from the exposed glacier. Attempts to evacuate him by helicopter were unsuccessful because of the severe weather. The rangers consequently remained with him through Monday night, spending a second night at approximately 12,500 feet alongside the injured climber.Meanwhile, the Siskiyou County Sheriff's Office mobilised more than 30 additional search-and-rescue personnel to carry out a ground evacuation. The operation required teams to negotiate steep terrain, loose rocks and hazardous mountain conditions as the man's condition worsened.Teen rescuers joined the difficult extractionAmong those involved were members of the Marin County Sheriff's Office Search and Rescue team, including young volunteers who took part in the demanding climb. According to reporting by SFGATE and KTVU, members of the team ascended the mountain carrying rescue equipment and used technical rope systems to manoeuvre the injured climber across steep, rocky sections. The rescuers transported him towards the saddle between Mount Shasta and neighbouring Shastina Peak, where a helicopter could potentially land.The ground operation was complicated by winds reaching 50 to 60 mph, freezing temperatures and the risk of rockfall. The teams had to work carefully across exposed terrain while trying to get the climber to a safer elevation. Additional rescue personnel reached the man on Tuesday afternoon and helped move him further down the mountain. During a brief improvement in the weather, a California Highway Patrol helicopter reached the team near Shastina Peak and airlifted the climber to safety.Mount Shasta's changing conditions raise safety concernsMount Shasta, in Northern California, is the state's fifth-highest peak and the second-highest in the Cascade Range. Although some routes are accessible to experienced hikers and climbers during favourable conditions, the mountain can become considerably more dangerous as winter weather approaches.The incident also highlights the risks of relying exclusively on electronic navigation when travelling through remote alpine terrain. An incorrect route can lead climbers onto glaciers or other areas where specialist equipment and technical skills are necessary. Officials recommend that climbers research their routes carefully, check seasonal conditions and carry suitable clothing, navigation backups, emergency supplies and equipment for snow and ice. Reaching the summit should never take priority over making a safe descent. The Florida climber's name and hometown have not been released publicly. His rescue brought an end to a multiday operation that required rescuers to endure the same freezing conditions and dangerous terrain while working to bring him off the mountain alive.You use AI every day. articles.body: Instagram head Adam Mosseri has said public frustration and anger over AI are likely to increase over the next few years, as concerns grow about job losses, content ownership and the impact of AI on creative industries. Speaking on the Colin and Samir podcast, Mosseri was asked about AI and the trend of college students booing tech CEOs at graduation ceremonies. Adam Mosseri replied saying that he expects to see more anger directed at AI, with the backlash extending beyond young people and content creators."It’s not only getting worse, it’s going to continue to get worse. I think we’re going to see more frustration and anger, some of it founded, some of it unfounded, over the next couple of years, and that’s going to make it hard for a lot of people, not just in the industry", he said.The reaction reflects wider concerns about how rapidly advancing AI tools could affect jobs, creative work and people's ability to keep up with technological change.Why people are increasingly frustrated with AIAdam Mosseri said the concerns surrounding AI go beyond the creative industry, with people worried about several aspects of the technology, including the possibility of losing their jobs and having their work used to train AI models."I think people are concerned about a lot of things. I think they’re concerned about owning their content and models getting trained on their content. I think they’re concerned— there’s people who are concerned about safety,” Mosseri said.“They’re concerned about job displacement, having AI displace whatever it is they do, if you’re a content creator or an engineer or a mathematician. I think there’s concerns about— I mean, fundamentally what I think it comes down to when you really have, like, a heart-to-heart with someone is a fear of being left behind in some way," he added.Mosseri also addressed how Instagram handles AI-generated content, distinguishing between the technology itself and the quality of the material being produced."There’s a lot of great AI content out there, there’s also a lot of AI slop. Do we rank AI content as well as we rank non-AI content? Probably not." He said the term AI "slop" is sometimes used too liberally, even as low-quality AI-generated material becomes a growing concern on social media platforms.Mosseri claimed Instagram does not rank AI creators differently. His comments suggest that the platform's approach to ranking content is linked to its quality rather than simply whether AI was used to create it.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Telangana HC orders reinstatement of 35 sacked junior lecturers
articles.summary: HYDERABAD: Telangana high court has suspended proceedings issued by the education department cancelling the appointment of 35 junior lecturers (JLs) and
articles.body: HYDERABAD: Telangana high court has suspended proceedings issued by the education department cancelling the appointment of 35 junior lecturers (JLs) and directed state govt to reinstate them in service forthwith, holding that their appointments cannot be cancelled over allegations of fake postgraduate certificates without conducting an inquiry and giving them an opportunity to defend themselves.Justice K Sarath passed the interim orders on Wednesday while hearing a batch of petitions challenging the Oct 1 proceedings issued by the director of Intermediate education. The judge also clarified that the interim order would not prevent the authorities from initiating departmental proceedings in accordance with law.According to the petitioners, their services were regularised in May 2023 along with over 3,000 contractual JLs after they submitted postgraduate certificates and genuineness letters issued by the respective universities.“The department initially accepted these documents but later issued show-cause notices alleging that their certificates were not genuine,” they argued.The petitioners submitted explanations denying the allegations and pointed out that the universities had earlier certified their qualifications as genuine.They argued that the authorities ignored their explanations and cancelled their appointments without conducting an inquiry under the applicable service rules.“Further, the director of Intermediate education, being a higher authority, could not bypass the regional joint director of Intermediate education, the disciplinary authority, thereby depriving them of an opportunity to appeal,” the petitioners added.Govt opposed the petitions, stating that the universities had informed the department that records relating to the lecturers’ certificates could not be found.“Their appointments were subject to verification of original certificates, their probation had not been declared and a regular departmental inquiry was not necessary before cancelling their appointments,” the govt counsel argued.In response, the court observed that the lecturers had produced university letters certifying the genuineness of their certificates, while subsequent communications from the same universities questioned their authenticity. “This discrepancy required an inquiry and an opportunity for the lecturers to explain their position,” the judge said.Relying on Supreme Court judgments, the court held that termination based on allegations of misconduct, which carries a stigma, cannot be treated as a simple discharge articles.title: US company’s patent bid for life-saving TB therapy nixed
articles.summary: GURGAON: The Indian Patent Office has rejected a patent application by US-based Global Alliance for TB Drug Development for BPaL, a life-saving
articles.body: GURGAON: The Indian Patent Office has rejected a patent application by US-based Global Alliance for TB Drug Development for BPaL, a life-saving tuberculosis therapy, citing lack of novelty and inventive step. The decision could allow domestic drugmakers to launch cheaper generic versions in India and other high-burden countries, health experts said.Govt provides BPaL, a combination of bedaquiline, pretomanid and linezolid, free under National TB Elimination Programme. However, treatment costs remain a challenge. The six-month all-oral regimen is shorter than older treatments and reduces patients’ compliance burden. More than 15,000 patients have begun BPaLM, which adds moxifloxacin, under the programme.Pre-grant oppositions were filed separately by Sankalp Rehabilitation Trust’s Eldred Tellis and TB survivor Ganesh Acharya, supported by Lawyers’ Collective and Médécins Sans Frontières Access Campaign; and Delhi Network of Positive People, supported by Third World Network.Patent Controller upheld grounds of lack of novelty, lack of inventive step, non-patentability and insufficient disclosure, refusing application under Sec 15 of Patents Act. Opponents argued the combination and its use in a shorter regimen had been disclosed in scientific research dating to 2015.The opposition invoked Sections 3(d), 3(e) and 3(i), which restrict patents on new uses of known substances, exclude mere admixtures and methods of medical treatment. All four grounds were upheld.TB Alliance had earlier licensed generic firms, including Macleods Pharma and Lupin, to manufacture pretomanid for BPaL in India, though health activists called the agreements restrictive. Witty banter, spontaneous plans and conversations that stretch late into the night are often what make a relationship exciting. This air sign enjoys a partner who is curious, communicative and willing to explore new experiences together. While romantic gestures are welcome, intellectual connection and playful communication are equally important. This Karwa Chauth, a heartfelt conversation, a fun date or a message that makes them smile could be the key to their heart.Love language: Words of affirmation and quality time.Cancer (June 21 – July 22): Reassurance Is the Ultimate RomanceSensitive, nurturing and deeply sentimental, Cancer often looks for emotional security in a relationship. They may remember the smallest details, cherish shared memories and express affection through thoughtful acts of care. For Cancer, romance is not necessarily about elaborate surprises; it is about knowing that their feelings matter and that their partner will show up when it counts. Compliments, thoughtful presents and a date planned with care can make Leo feel special. However, beneath their confident exterior is someone who also wants their efforts to be recognised. articles.title: In the 1950s, Florida’s pet trade imported South American caimans; decades later, they were competing with native crocodilians in Everglades wetlands
articles.summary: Explore the impact of spectacled caimans introduced in the 1950s on Florida's native crocodilian species and the challenges they pose to the Everglades ecosystem.
articles.body: Florida’s wetlands contain a combination of native reptile species; none is more emblematic of the state than the American alligator. The Everglades also contain the American crocodile, which has a more limited coastal distribution, so two crocodilian species are found together in that area, sharing the same waters, food sources and nesting grounds. Their existence relies on factors such as water levels, salinity, food and habitat. Florida is a major hub for the exotic pet trade, especially in South Florida, where importers, breeders and tourist attractions are involved. Some exotic pets are later released by owners, contributing to the spread of non-native species. Some escape from captivity while others are simply released and in a warm climate with canals and ponds in Southern Florida, a few survive and reproduce.Pet shop popularity in the 1950s after restrictions on the alligator tradeA review titled The invasive spectacled caiman (Caiman crocodilus) in Florida, United States: invasion timeline, insights, and implications for Everglades restoration, published in Frontiers in Amphibian and Reptile Science on April 6, 2026, reports that spectacled caimans became popular in the American pet trade in the 1950s after restrictions on the American alligator trade. Most caimans imported since then came from Colombia, which made it the main source of the animals introduced in Florida. The species is a mid-sized crocodilian that rarely exceeds 2.5 m in total length and adapts to a wide variety of habitats. The species’ rapid establishment in South Florida likely reflected a large initial founder population, small-bodied reproductive animals, broad habitat tolerance and warm temperatures and the authors warn that spread into protected areas such as Everglades National Park could make control harder and increase the risk to sensitive ecosystems.First wild records in the 1960s and an established populationThe review reports that the earliest wild sightings of spectacled caimans in Florida date to the 1960s, when residents reported them in Palm Beach County. In the 1970s, caimans were first found and removed at Homestead Air Reserve Base and by 1980 the species was determined to be established, meaning it was reproducing in the wild in South Florida. These dates mark when wild animals were recorded, not when they arrived. The Wildlife Society’s summary of another removal study places the introductions mainly in and around Homestead in the 1950s, the decade the pet trade took off.330,705 caimans imported into the United States between 1977 and 2024The review also traces the trade. CITES trade data show 330,705 spectacled caimans imported into the United States from 1977 to 2024, so the total does not cover the earlier imports of the 1950s and 1960s. U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service LEMIS records show 18,525 caimans imported directly into Florida from 1999 to 2018, with a peak of 10,841 in 1999 and a low of 6 in 2018 and Guyana was the largest source at 12,211. The species is not listed as prohibited in Florida, so importation, trade, possession and breeding remain allowed under Florida statutes 379.3761 and 379.3762.Habitat overlap with alligators in Biscayne BayThe review claims that caimans in South Florida inhabit canals, ponds and ditches, but recent reports of their presence have been in marsh and slough habitats within Water Conservation Area 3 and Everglades National Park, such as Shark River Slough. The 2023 study What is the potential for extirpating spectacled caiman from Comprehensive Everglades Restoration Plan projects in South Florida?, published in Management of Biological Invasions, used survey and removal data from 2012 to 2021 along 11 survey routes.Its authors removed 251 caimans over that period and annual removals rose from 5 in 2012 to a peak of 47 in 2020. The review credits the same study with placing nesting from mid-June to mid-July and the start of hatching in early September.Competition with native crocodilians remains a hypothesisThe review is cautious on this point. Competition among caimans, alligators and crocodiles remains hypothetical and has not been quantified, and the authors call for research on how far the species’ niches overlap. They suggest that large caiman populations could limit the recovery of native crocodilians and hamper Everglades restoration goals. They point to the Amazon basin, where evidence suggests spectacled caimans may be limiting the recovery of black caimans and to Venezuela, where their expansion is hypothesized to have inhibited the reintroduction of Orinoco crocodiles.You use AI every day. articles.title: Judge named accused in son’s fatal Mercedes crash gets interim protection from arrest
articles.summary: KOCHI: The Kerala high court on Thursday granted interim protection from arrest to the additional district judge whose 17-year-old son allegedly drove a
articles.body: KOCHI: The Kerala high court on Thursday granted interim protection from arrest to the additional district judge whose 17-year-old son allegedly drove a Mercedes-Benz that hit a two-wheeler in Kochi, killing the rider.Justice Kauser Edappagath passed the order on an anticipatory bail plea filed by the judge, who is posted at a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal in Irinjalakuda, Thrissur district.“The police shall not arrest the applicant until further orders. However, he shall appear before the investigating officer today at 1pm and if necessary as and when called for. The interrogation of the applicant shall be done in accordance with the guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court,” the court ordered.Senior advocate P Vijaya Bhanu, appearing for the judge, told the court that his client had appeared before the police on Wednesday and was interrogated for more than four hours. Another notice directing him to appear before the police had since been issued.Questioning the need for further interrogation and custodial questioning, the court remarked, “What was the need to interrogate him for four hours and now for further interrogation? Why is his arrest required? He is a judicial officer. He will co-operate with the investigation.”Counsel representing the victim’s legal heirs opposed the plea, alleging that the judge had tampered with evidence after being informed of the accident.The court said it had to proceed strictly in accordance with the law and granted interim protection from arrest. It also asked the prosecutor to provide the state’s response to the plea.The judge was named as an accused in the FIR registered after the October 25 crash in Cheranalloor, Kochi, in which his minor son allegedly drove the car that hit a two-wheeler, killing Jayabalakrishnan.In his anticipatory bail plea, the judge claimed he had no knowledge that the vehicle had been taken from the premises. He said he learnt of the accident after receiving a phone call while asleep.The plea also argued that Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder, requires knowledge that the act is likely to cause death.Meanwhile, the victim’s family has complained to the Kerala high court chief justice seeking an inquiry into the judicial officer’s conduct.
